claim: Expansion microscopy (ExM) achieves nanoscale-precise imaging of specimens at ~70 nm resolution with ~4.5x linear expansion.
source: We recently developed expansion microscopy (ExM), which achieves nanoscale-precise imaging of specimens at ~70 nm resolution (with ~4.5x linear expansion) by isotropic swelling of chemically processed, hydrogel-embedded tissue.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the resolution and expansion factor of ExM.

claim: ExM of C. elegans is challenged by its cuticle, which is stiff and impermeable to antibodies.
source: ExM of C. elegans is challenged by its cuticle, which is stiff and impermeable to antibodies.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract identifying a technical challenge.

claim: ExCel enables simultaneous readout of fluorescent proteins, RNA, DNA location, and anatomical structures at resolutions of ~65–75 nm (3.3–3.8x linear expansion).
source: ExCel enables simultaneous readout of fluorescent proteins, RNA, DNA location, and anatomical structures at resolutions of ~65–75 nm (3.3–3.8x linear expansion).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the capabilities and resolution of ExCel.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel enables imaging of endogenous proteins stained by antibodies.
source: We also developed epitope-preserving ExCel, which enables imaging of endogenous proteins stained by antibodies
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing a variant of ExCel.

claim: Iterative ExCel enables imaging of fluorescent proteins after 20x linear expansion.
source: and iterative ExCel, which enables imaging of fluorescent proteins after 20x linear expansion.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing another variant of ExCel.

claim: C. elegans has 959 somatic cells in adult hermaphrodites.
source: Caenorhabditis elegans is an important model system in biology, because of its tractable size (959 somatic cells in adult hermaphrodites)
evidence: This is a direct statement providing a known biological fact about C. elegans.

claim: Super-resolution microscopy methods including STORM, PALM, SR-SIM, and STED have been applied to C. elegans.
source: Perhaps not surprisingly, therefore, super-resolution microscopy has been useful to the analysis of C. elegans, with studies applying STORM, PALM, SR-SIM, and STED to C. elegans to investigate cells and tissues in both intact or dissected C. elegans (Rankin et al., 2011; Gao et al., 2012; Vangindertael et al., 2015; He et al., 2016; Köhler et al., 2017; Krieg et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The depths of imaging of super-resolution studies in C. elegans were largely physically limited to a few microns to tens of microns.
source: However, the depths of imaging of such studies were largely physically limited to a few microns to tens of microns, insufficient to map the entire depth of an adult animal
evidence: This statement describes a limitation of prior super-resolution methods based on cited studies.

claim: The tough cuticle of C. elegans presents a barrier to immunostaining in the intact animal.
source: Furthermore, the tough cuticle of C. elegans presents a barrier to immunostaining in the intact animal, important for STORM and STED imaging and for the general labeling of proteins in a variety of scientific contexts.
evidence: This is a statement about a known biological property of C. elegans.

claim: Expansion microscopy (ExM) involves isotropically expanding biological specimens by permeating them with a swellable hydrogel polymer network.
source: Recently, we discovered that it is possible to isotropically expand biological specimens by permeating them evenly and densely with a swellable hydrogel polymer network, anchoring key biomolecules or labels to the hydrogel, softening the tissue through a chemical process, and then adding water, which swells the polymer and in turn the tissue (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement describes the ExM technique with a citation to the original work.

claim: ExM has been applied to tissues of mice, human patients, and in many other biological contexts.
source: This technique, expansion microscopy (ExM), is now being adapted and improved by many groups, and has been applied to tissues of mice, human patients, and in many other biological contexts (Chen et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016; Chozinski et al., 2016; Ku et al., 2016; Tillberg et al., 2016; Chang et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2017; Park, 2018; Truckenbrodt et al., 2018; Gambarotto et al., 2019; Wassie et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The C. elegans cuticle is impermeable to many small molecules and all antibodies.
source: However, C. elegans is wrapped in a multi-layer cuticle, which is well known to be impermeable to many small molecules and all antibodies, and mechanically stiff to the point where physical expansion would be expected to proceed poorly (Duerr, 2006; Page and Johnstone, 2007; Chisholm and Xu, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work on C. elegans cuticle properties.

claim: The C. elegans cuticle is mechanically stiff.
source: However, C. elegans is wrapped in a multi-layer cuticle, which is well known to be impermeable to many small molecules and all antibodies, and mechanically stiff to the point where physical expansion would be expected to proceed poorly (Duerr, 2006; Page and Johnstone, 2007; Chisholm and Xu, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work on C. elegans cuticle properties.

claim: ExCel results in low-distortion (~1–6% over length scales of 0–100 μm) physical expansion by ~3.3x.
source: This protocol results in high signal-to-background antibody staining against protease-resistant fluorescent proteins, low-distortion (~1–6% over length scales of 0–100 μm) physical expansion by ~3.3x, and both protein and RNA detection with sub-cellular resolution.
evidence: This statement describes measured properties of the ExCel protocol.

claim: ExCel enables both protein and RNA detection with sub-cellular resolution.
source: This protocol results in high signal-to-background antibody staining against protease-resistant fluorescent proteins, low-distortion (~1–6% over length scales of 0–100 μm) physical expansion by ~3.3x, and both protein and RNA detection with sub-cellular resolution.
evidence: This statement describes capabilities of the ExCel protocol.

claim: ExCel enables simultaneous imaging of proteins, RNA, and DNA location within the same specimen.
source: Using ExCel, we were able to resolve synaptic and gap junction proteins better than with ordinary confocal microscopy, and simultaneously image proteins, RNA, and DNA location within the same specimen.
evidence: This statement describes demonstrated capabilities of ExCel.

claim: Multiplexed capability for imaging multiple molecular types has not been demonstrated with previous super-resolution methods in C. elegans.
source: In particular, such multiplexed capability has not been demonstrated with previous super-resolution methods in C. elegans, and facilitates nanoscale-precise analyses of how multiple molecular types are spatially organized in the context of an entire animal.
evidence: This statement compares ExCel capabilities to prior methods.

claim: Standard ExCel visualizes fluorescent reporters, such as those fused to proteins of interest, which requires transgenesis.
source: The standard ExCel protocol visualizes fluorescent reporters, such as those fused to proteins of interest, which requires transgenesis, and could in principle affect the function and localization of the target protein.
evidence: This statement describes a limitation of the standard ExCel protocol.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel enables detection of untagged, completely endogenous proteins using off-the-shelf primary antibodies.
source: Thus, we additionally developed an alternative ExCel protocol, which we call epitope-preserving ExCel, that enables detection of untagged, completely endogenous proteins, using off-the-shelf primary antibodies.
evidence: This statement describes a capability of epitope-preserving ExCel.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel replaces Proteinase K with an epitope-preserving cuticle-permeabilization treatment.
source: The epitope-preserving ExCel protocol replaces the use of Proteinase K, a general protease that disrupts most epitopes in the standard ExCel protocol, with an epitope-preserving cuticle-permeabilization treatment that we identified in a systematic screen of chemical treatments.
evidence: This statement describes a methodological difference between protocols.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel has a slightly reduced expansion factor (~2.8x) compared to standard ExCel.
source: This protocol enables antibody staining of protein epitopes at the expense of a slightly reduced expansion factor (~2.8x) and lower expansion isotropy (~8–25% error over length scales of 0–100 μm).
evidence: This statement describes measured properties of epitope-preserving ExCel.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel has lower expansion isotropy (~8–25% error over length scales of 0–100 μm) compared to standard ExCel.
source: This protocol enables antibody staining of protein epitopes at the expense of a slightly reduced expansion factor (~2.8x) and lower expansion isotropy (~8–25% error over length scales of 0–100 μm).
evidence: This statement describes measured properties of epitope-preserving ExCel.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel was used to identify a previously unreported protein localization at the junctions between developing vulval precursor cells.
source: We showed that epitope-preserving ExCel allows multiplexed readout of multiple native proteins at super-resolution, a capability that we used to identify a previously unreported protein localization at the junctions between developing vulval precursor cells
evidence: This statement describes a specific finding using epitope-preserving ExCel.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel was used to resolve the peri-active and active zones of chemical pre-synapses.
source: and to resolve the peri-active and active zones of chemical pre-synapses.
evidence: This statement describes a specific finding using epitope-preserving ExCel.

claim: Iterative ExCel (iExCel) enables two successive rounds of hydrogel-mediated expansion.
source: Lastly, we developed a third protocol, iterative ExCel (iExCel), which enables two successive rounds of hydrogel-mediated expansion of a given worm, by incorporating the previously validated strategies of iterative expansion microscopy into the ExCel context (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement describes the iExCel protocol with a citation to prior work.

claim: iExCel brings the expansion factor from ~4x to ~4x × ~4x = ~20x.
source: iExCel brings the expansion factor from ~4x to ~4x *~4x = ~20x, and the theoretical limit of resolution down to ~25 nm
evidence: This statement describes the expansion factor achieved by iExCel.

claim: iExCel achieves a theoretical limit of resolution down to ~25 nm.
source: iExCel brings the expansion factor from ~4x to ~4x *~4x = ~20x, and the theoretical limit of resolution down to ~25 nm
evidence: This statement describes the resolution achieved by iExCel.

claim: iExCel has low distortion (~1.5–4.5% over length scales of 0–100 μm), on par with standard ExCel.
source: at a low level of distortion (~1.5–4.5% over length scales of 0–100 μm), on par with that of standard ExCel, on which it builds.
evidence: This statement describes measured properties of iExCel.

claim: With iExCel, fluorescent puncta that may represent individual GFP molecules expressed in the neuronal cytosol were resolved.
source: With iExCel, we were able to resolve fluorescent puncta that may represent individual GFP molecules expressed in the neuronal cytosol.
evidence: This statement describes a specific finding using iExCel.

claim: Challenges remaining in deploying ExM in C. elegans include distortion in the gonad and mouth regions.
source: Each of these ExCel protocols highlights some of the challenges remaining in deploying ExM in C. elegans, including distortion in the gonad and mouth regions, reduced general isotropy with epitope-preserving ExCel, and the ability to only detect fluorescent proteins with the current form of iExCel
evidence: This statement identifies limitations of the current protocols.

claim: The current form of iExCel can only detect fluorescent proteins.
source: and the ability to only detect fluorescent proteins with the current form of iExCel
evidence: This statement identifies a limitation of iExCel.

claim: In protein retention ExM (proExM), a formaldehyde fixed specimen is labeled with fluorescent antibodies.
source: In one popular form of ExM, protein retention ExM (proExM; Tillberg et al., 2016), a formaldehyde fixed specimen is labeled with fluorescent antibodies
evidence: This statement describes a step in the proExM protocol with a citation.

claim: In proExM, the sample is treated with a protein-binding anchor, AcX, which equips proteins with a polymer-binding handle.
source: and then the sample is treated with a protein-binding anchor, AcX, which equips the proteins (including the fluorescent antibodies) with a polymer-binding handle
evidence: This statement describes a step in the proExM protocol.

claim: In proExM, the sample is evenly permeated by the monomer sodium acrylate plus a crosslinker.
source: then the sample is evenly permeated by the monomer sodium acrylate (plus a crosslinker).
evidence: This statement describes a step in the proExM protocol.

claim: In proExM, monomers self-assemble into a dense polymer matrix, a hydrogel of swellable sodium polyacrylate.
source: The monomers self-assemble into a dense polymer matrix, a hydrogel of swellable sodium polyacrylate, to which AcX (and thus proteins) are bound.
evidence: This statement describes a step in the proExM protocol.

claim: In proExM, treatment with Proteinase K softens the sample by destroying most proteins, but sparing the fluorescent antibodies.
source: Treatment with a strong protease, Proteinase K, softens the sample by destroying most proteins, but sparing the fluorescent antibodies.
evidence: This statement describes a step in the proExM protocol.

claim: In proExM, adding water swells the hydrogel-specimen composite by ~4.5x in linear extent for mouse brain specimens.
source: Then, adding water swells the hydrogel-specimen composite by ~4.5x in linear extent, for mouse brain specimens.
evidence: This statement describes the expansion achieved in proExM for a specific tissue type.

claim: ExFISH uses an RNA-binding anchor, LabelX, to couple RNA molecules to the hydrogel.
source: A related process, expansion microscopy followed by in situ hybridization (ExFISH; Chen et al., 2016), uses an RNA-binding anchor, LabelX, to couple RNA molecules to the hydrogel, with similar monomer-infusion and proteolysis steps as proExM.
evidence: This statement describes the ExFISH protocol with a citation.

claim: Animals are fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min at room temperature, and then for 4 hr at 4°C in the ExCel protocol.
source: We fix animals with 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min at room temperature, and then for 4 hr at 4°C (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement describes a specific step in the ExCel protocol.

claim: Animals are incubated in a buffer containing 2% β-mercaptoethanol overnight at 4°C to chemically reduce disulfide bonds between collagen fibers in the cuticle.
source: We then incubate the animals in a buffer containing 2% β-mercaptoethanol overnight at 4°C to chemically reduce the disulfide bonds between collagen fibers in the cuticle, as in Finney and Ruvkun (1990), Garriga et al. (1993), and Duerr (2006) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This statement describes a specific step in the ExCel protocol with citations to prior work.

claim: The AcX treatment is performed with a low-pH buffer (pH 6.0 MBST) to help with deep AcX permeation into specimens.
source: The AcX treatment is performed with a low-pH buffer (pH 6.0 MBST, i.e. MES-buffer saline with Triton X-100) building from our prior observation that such a condition helped with deep AcX permeation into specimens (Tillberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes a design choice in the ExCel protocol with a citation to prior work.

claim: Samples are pre-incubated with non-activated monomer solution overnight at 4°C to ensure equilibration of monomer concentration.
source: We then perform monomer infusion (Figure 1F) by incubating the specimen in non-activated monomer solution (7.5% (w/w) sodium acrylate, 2.5% (w/w) acrylamide, 0.5% (w/w) N,N'-diallyl-tartardiamide (DATD; a crosslinker that can be chemically cleaved by periodate ions [Späth and Koblet, 1979], which we reasoned would make the hydrogel compatible with ExM-related downstream applications that require the disintegration of this initial hydrogel; we employ this hydrogel-disintegration procedure in two other C. elegans expansion protocols that we describe later in this manuscript), in a solution of 50 mM MOPS pH 7.0 and 2 M NaCl) overnight at 4°C. We reasoned that this overnight incubation could promote more thorough diffusion of hydrogel monomers into the specimen, compared to the 30 min incubation in the published proExM or ExFISH protocols.
evidence: This statement describes a design choice in the ExCel protocol with reasoning.

claim: DATD is a crosslinker that can be chemically cleaved by periodate ions.
source: 0.5% (w/w) N,N'-diallyl-tartardiamide (DATD; a crosslinker that can be chemically cleaved by periodate ions [Späth and Koblet, 1979]
evidence: This statement describes a chemical property with a citation.

claim: An extensive Proteinase K digestion over 2 days at 37°C is performed to allow thorough digestion of the cuticle.
source: an extensive Proteinase K digestion over 2 days at 37°C (Figure 1H), longer than in previous protocols (Chen et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016; Tillberg et al., 2016; Chang et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2017), to allow a thorough digestion of the cuticle.
evidence: This statement describes a design choice in the ExCel protocol with citations to prior work.

claim: A digestion buffer containing 40 mM CaCl2 is used to prevent premature hydrogel expansion during the digestion process.
source: To prevent premature hydrogel expansion during the digestion process, we designed a digestion buffer containing 40 mM CaCl2, since such divalent cations prevent polyacrylate gel expansion (Tillberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes a design choice in the ExCel protocol with a citation.

claim: Divalent cations prevent polyacrylate gel expansion.
source: since such divalent cations prevent polyacrylate gel expansion (Tillberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes a chemical property with a citation.

claim: Specimens are partially expanded in 6 serial washes lasting 30 min each, incrementally reducing salt concentrations.
source: Thus, we designed a protocol to partially expand the Proteinase K digested specimens in 6 serial washes lasting 30 min each, incrementally reducing salt concentrations each time (i.e., lowering Tris, NaCl, and CaCl2 concentrations bit by bit throughout each of the 6 washes, ending with 5x saline-sodium citrate buffer (SSC)) (Figure 1I).
evidence: This statement describes a design choice in the ExCel protocol.

claim: The final expansion factor at the end of the 6 washes is 1.8-fold.
source: The final expansion factor at the end of the 6 washes is 1.8-fold.
evidence: This statement describes a measured property of the ExCel protocol.

claim: The original proExM protocol preserves, to some extent, fluorescent proteins.
source: Although the original proExM protocol preserves, to some extent, fluorescent proteins (Tillberg et al., 2016), some of the fluorescent proteins are destroyed, a problem exacerbated by a strong Proteinase K digestion protocol such as utilized here.
evidence: This statement describes a property of the proExM protocol with a citation.

claim: Fluorescent antibodies that bind to remaining fluorescent proteins are added to amplify their fluorescence.
source: We thus add fluorescent antibodies that bind to the remaining fluorescent proteins, to amplify their fluorescence (Figure 1J)
evidence: This statement describes a step in the ExCel protocol.

claim: NHS ester of a fluorescent dye binds to amines and enables visualization of general anatomical features.
source: We next perform optional steps, such as the adding of an N-hydroxysuccinimide ester (NHS ester) of a fluorescent dye, which binds to amines and thus enables the visualization of general anatomical features
evidence: This statement describes a chemical property and its application.

claim: DAPI is added to visualize DNA location.
source: or the adding of DAPI to visualize DNA location (Figure 1K).
evidence: This statement describes a step in the ExCel protocol.

claim: The final specimen is expanded by ~3.8-fold in deionized water.
source: Finally, we expand the tissue-hydrogel composite yet further, again at a slow speed by using four serial washes of 30 min each, reducing the amount of SSC each time, until the final specimen is immersed in deionized water (Figure 1L). This results in a final expansion of 3.8-fold.
evidence: This statement describes a measured property of the ExCel protocol.

claim: 0.05x SSC promotes stability of antibody staining signals better than deionized water.
source: However, we found that 0.05x SSC, i.e. a low-salt environment, promotes stability of antibody staining signals better than deionized water, i.e. a no-salt environment, and may be favorable for long-term (>1–3 hr) imaging
evidence: This statement describes an observation from the experiments.

claim: The final expansion factor in 0.05x SSC is 3.3-fold.
source: to reach this state, we skip the last wash (with deionized water) in the serial washes, so the final specimen ends up immersed in 0.05x SSC, with a final expansion factor of 3.3-fold.
evidence: This statement describes a measured property of the ExCel protocol.

claim: The original ExFISH protocol achieved a linear expansion factor of ~3.3x for mouse brain specimens.
source: In the original ExFISH protocol, a linear expansion factor of ~3.3x was achieved, for mouse brain specimens.
evidence: This statement describes a property of the ExFISH protocol.

claim: Version 3.0 HCR strategies use split-initiator probes that carry half the HCR initiator length of previous versions.
source: However, newer ('version 3.0') HCR strategies, which offer higher signal-to-background ratio and reduced necessity of optimizing probe sequences on a per-RNA-target-basis (Choi et al., 2018) use split-initiator probes that carry half the HCR initiator length of previous versions of HCR probes (18 instead of 36 nucleotides)
evidence: This statement describes a property of HCR version 3.0 with a citation.

claim: ExCel enables good antibody access to the inside of C. elegans.
source: We observed bright, uniform anti-GFP staining of the nervous system in ExCel-processed, but not pre-ExCel, animals (Figure 2A), suggesting that ExCel could enable good antibody access to the inside of C. elegans
evidence: This statement is supported by observations from Figure 2A.

claim: GFP epitopes can survive Proteinase K digestion sufficiently to serve as targets for antibody labeling.
source: and that GFP epitopes could survive the Proteinase K digestion sufficiently to serve as targets for antibody labeling.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the observation of successful antibody staining.

claim: Signal-to-background ratios obtained with ExCel were several fold higher than those obtained using prior immunohistochemistry protocols.
source: Signal-to-background ratios obtained with ExCel were several fold higher than those obtained using prior immunohistochemistry protocols (Finney and Ruvkun, 1990; Li and Chalfie, 1990; Nonet et al., 1997; Duerr, 2006; Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and D with citations to prior protocols.

claim: ExCel works for fluorescent proteins including GFP, mCherry, and TagRFP.
source: ExCel worked not just for GFP, but also worked for other fluorescent proteins such as mCherry and TagRFP (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: NHS esters of fluorescent dyes can be applied to ExCel-processed animals to support single-color identification of many anatomical features.
source: Thus, as a novel tissue staining strategy, NHS esters of fluorescent dyes can be applied to ExCel-processed animals to support single-color identification of many anatomical features, which could in turn provide spatial context for other biological signals.
evidence: This statement is supported by observations from Figure 4.

claim: Simultaneous readout of GFP, the mRNA of GFP, DNA and anatomical features can be achieved with ExCel.
source: We observed that simultaneous readout of GFP, the mRNA of GFP, DNA and anatomical features could be achieved (Figure 5, Video 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5 and Video 3.

claim: ExCel resolved nearby puncta that were blurred into a single punctum at the pre-ExCel stage.
source: ExCel resolved nearby puncta that were blurred into a single punctum at the pre-ExCel stage (Figure 6A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 2.1-fold more puncta were detected in post-ExCel images than in pre-ExCel images.
source: and observed 2.1-fold more detected puncta in post-ExCel images than in pre-ExCel images (Figure 6C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: CHE-7::TagRFP can be clearly visualized after ExCel.
source: We observed that CHE-7::TagRFP can be clearly visualized after ExCel, and that its appearance corresponds nearly identically between pre-ExCel and post-ExCel states (Figure 7B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: ExCel has sufficient sensitivity to detect fluorescent-reporter-tagged proteins expressed at endogenous levels.
source: Thus, ExCel has sufficient sensitivity to detect fluorescent-reporter-tagged proteins expressed at endogenous levels, and can potentially facilitate mapping of both chemical and electrical synapses in the C. elegans nervous system.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the observation of CHE-7::TagRFP detection.

claim: Nearly all egfp mRNA were localized inside GFP neurons.
source: As a positive control, we confirmed that nearly all egfp mRNA were localized inside GFP neurons (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The mRNA of parvalbumin, a mammalian GABAergic neuronal protein with no known orthologs in C. elegans, was not detectable in C. elegans.
source: As a negative control, we found that the mRNA of parvalbumin, a mammalian GABAergic neuronal protein with no known orthologs in C. elegans (Hobert, 2013), was not detectable in C. elegans (Figure 8B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 8B with a citation.

claim: For all probed targets, the vast majority (~80–100%) of the ExFISH-HCR signal was detected inside neurons.
source: For all of the probed targets, we observed that the vast majority (~80–100%) of the ExFISH-HCR signal was detected inside neurons (GFP-filled regions).
evidence: This statement is supported by observations from Figure 8.

claim: The vast majority (~80–90%) of transcripts were found in the peri-nuclear space of the cell body.
source: For all the mRNA transcripts that we imaged, we observed that the vast majority (~80–90%) of transcripts were found in the peri-nuclear space of the cell body (Figure 9A, Video 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9A and Video 4.

claim: A relatively small number of transcripts (~5–20%) were observed in the nuclei, which may indicate transcription sites.
source: Overall, we observed a relatively small number of transcripts (~5–20%) in the nuclei, which may indicate transcription sites (Ji and van Oudenaarden, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by observations with a citation.

claim: Nearly no transcripts were detected inside the nerve ring.
source: As a related observation, nearly no transcripts were detected inside the nerve ring (Figure 9B), which is a dense bundle of neural processes and does not contain neuronal soma (Zallen et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 9B with a citation.

claim: The expression of the same transcript could differ up to 3.9-fold in expressing neurons.
source: We observed that the expression of the same transcript could differ up to 3.9-fold in expressing neurons, as in the case of unc-25 mRNA molecule count in RIS (188.3 + / - 72.5; mean + / - standard deviation; n = 3 animals from 1 population) and RMED (48.7 + / - 20.5, mean + / - standard deviation; n = 3 animals from 1 population).
evidence: This statement is supported by data from single-neuron RNA quantification.

claim: No significant difference was observed in the expression levels of examined transcripts between L and R neurons of the same class.
source: We did not observe any significant difference in the expression levels of examined transcripts between L and R neurons of the same class, including unc-25 levels in RMEL/R (Figure 10D), cat-2 levels in ADEL/R (Figure 10E) and tph-1 levels in NSML/R (Figure 10F) (n = 3–7 animals from 1 population for each transcript; 2-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test; alpha = 0.05)
evidence: This statement is supported by statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 10D-F.

claim: A significant difference in unc-25 transcript count was observed between RMEV/D and RMEL/R neurons.
source: However, when we examined the RME neurons (a class of radially symmetric neurons) inside the same animals, we observed a significant difference in unc-25 transcript count between RMEV/D and RMEL/R neurons (Figure 10D, n = 6 neurons for each sub-class neuron group, over 3 animals from 1 population; p<0.01, two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test)
evidence: This statement is supported by statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: The combination of Coll VII and MAP5 treatments resulted in strong signal-to-noise ratios and expected patterns of localization for many epitope targets.
source: In summary, the combination of Coll VII and MAP5 treatments resulted in strong signal-to-noise ratios and expected patterns of localization for many epitope targets (Figure 12C)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 12C.

claim: The Coll VII/MAP5 dual treatment enables immunostaining of general epitopes in hydrogel-embedded, morphology-intact whole animals of C. elegans.
source: Thus, the Coll VII/MAP5 dual treatment enables immunostaining of general epitopes in hydrogel-embedded, morphology-intact whole animals of C. elegans.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion from the antibody screen results.

claim: The post-re-embedding iExCel sample gains additional expansion (from 3.6x to 4.6x) during the hybridization step.
source: During this hybridization step, the re-embedded sample swells by ~30% linearly, and results in a linear expansion factor of ~4.6x.
evidence: This statement describes a measured property of the iExCel protocol.

claim: The error over 0 to 100 microns was ~1.5–4.5% for animals across developmental stages from L1 to day 1 adulthood with iExCel.
source: We observed that the error over 0 to 100 microns was ~1.5–4.5% for animals across developmental stages from L1 to day 1 adulthood, which are within a similar range to that from standard ExCel (~1–6%), a single-round expansion protocol.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 18—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 2-round-expanded image clearly resolves individual fluorescent puncta that likely arose from individual GFP molecules.
source: Consequently, when we examined regions of the animal over the length scales of single neurons (Figure 18C) or over length scales of sub-neuron compartments (Figure 18D; showing a neuronal projection and a portion of a soma), we observed that the 2-round-expanded image clearly resolves individual fluorescent puncta (which likely arose from individual GFP molecules
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 18C-D.

claim: iExCel enables visualization of fluorescent proteins following iterative expansion of intact animals, for ~20x linear expansion factor and ~25 nm effective resolution.
source: Thus, iExCel enables visualization of fluorescent proteins following iterative expansion of intact animals, for ~20x linear expansion factor and ~25 nm effective resolution, which is demonstrated here to be finer than the inter-molecule distance for an over-expressed protein target in the cytosol.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion from the iExCel results.

claim: DYN-1 co-localizes with DLG-1 at cell-cell contact sites between vulval precursor cells.
source: While we observed that DLG-1 staining clearly localizes to the interface between neighboring vulval precursor cells, which has been described before (Shin and Reiner, 2018), we additionally detected that DYN-1 co-localizes with DLG-1 at these cell-cell contact sites (Figure 15F), which has not been directly reported in the past.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 15F with a citation to prior work.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel achieves the detection of, and the analysis of nanometer-scale spatial relationships between, untagged endogenous proteins within a chemical pre-synapse.
source: Thus, epitope-preserving ExCel achieves the detection of, and the analysis of nanometer-scale spatial relationships between, untagged endogenous proteins within a chemical pre-synapse.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion from the epitope-preserving ExCel results.

claim: DYN-1 shows a more diffuse localization than UNC-10, which forms sharper puncta but occupies less volume spatially.
source: We observed that both DYN-1 and UNC-10 densely localized to the nerve ring and the nerve cords, a pattern that is consistent with pre-re-embedded images (Figure 12C), but we additionally observed, at this post-expansion resolution, that DYN-1 and UNC-10 occupy spatially distinct sites (Figure 16C), with DYN-1 (the putative peri-active zone marker) showing a more diffuse localization than UNC-10 (the putative active zone marker), which forms sharper puncta but occupies less volume spatially.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 16C.

claim: UNC-10 puncta are spatially embedded amidst DYN-1 densities.
source: The UNC-10 puncta are spatially embedded amidst DYN-1 densities, which is reminiscent of observations made in other organisms, including lamprey, fruit fly and mouse, that the active zones are spatially surrounded by peri-active zones (Marie et al., 2004; Brodin and Shupliakov, 2006; Wahl et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 16D with citations to prior work.

claim: For synapses at the frontal end of the dorsal nerve cord, UNC-10 exclusively localizes to the ventral side of DYN-1, by distances of less than 0.5 micron.
source: At this resolution, we also noticed that for synapses at the frontal end of the dorsal nerve cord, UNC-10 exclusively localizes to the ventral side (i.e. facing the internal tissue) of DYN-1, by distances of less than 0.5 micron (Figure 16E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 16E.

claim: All three variants of ExCel offer the ability to image at arbitrary depths in the worm.
source: Compared to earlier super-resolution methods, all three variants of ExCel offer the ability to image at arbitrary depths in the worm, and on existing common microscopes available to many groups already.
evidence: This statement is a comparison to prior methods.

claim: The current standard of C. elegans in situ RNA detection, single-molecule FISH (smFISH), is diffraction-limited and requires wide-field illumination.
source: The current standard of C. elegans in situ RNA detection, single-molecule FISH (smFISH), is diffraction-limited and requires wide-field illumination (Ji and van Oudenaarden, 2012), yielding single transcript sizes of ~200–500 nm laterally, and ~700–800 nm axially.
evidence: This statement describes properties of smFISH with a citation.

claim: smFISH can practically detect up to ~10–20 transcripts in an average-sized neuronal soma before losing single-transcript resolution.
source: Given the small neuronal size of C. elegans, smFISH can practically detect up to ~10–20 transcripts in an average-sized neuronal soma before losing single-transcript resolution.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the resolution limits of smFISH and neuronal size.

claim: Standard-ExCel-based ExFISH-HCR can detect at least 300 individually resolvable transcripts at ~3.3x linear expansion.
source: On the other hand, standard-ExCel-based ExFISH-HCR can detect at least 300 individually resolvable transcripts at ~3.3x linear expansion (which reduces the effective size of HCR amplified transcripts to ~150 nm laterally, and ~250 nm axially)
evidence: This statement describes a capability of ExCel-based ExFISH-HCR.

claim: The standard ExCel is the only ExCel variant that currently supports RNA readout.
source: We note that out of the three variants of ExCel, the standard ExCel is the only one that currently supports RNA readout.
evidence: This statement describes a limitation of the other ExCel variants.

claim: The epitope-preserving ExCel uses a heat-mediated denaturation treatment at pH 9.0, which could induce alkaline hydrolysis of RNA molecules.
source: The epitope-preserving ExCel uses a heat-mediated denaturation treatment at pH 9.0, which could induce alkaline hydrolysis of RNA molecules and disrupt downstream detection.
evidence: This statement explains why epitope-preserving ExCel is incompatible with RNA readout.

claim: Eggshells of C. elegans embryos and the pharyngeal lumen walls both contain chitin.
source: Given that eggshells of C. elegans embryos (inside adult gonads) and the pharyngeal lumen walls (inside the mouth region) both contain chitin (Heustis et al., 2012; Stein and Golden, 2018), and are the only structures reported to contain chitin in C. elegans (Zhang et al., 2005)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Future versions of ExCel that incorporate chitin disruption may be able to alleviate distortions in the gonad and mouth areas.
source: it is possible that future versions of ExCel that incorporate chitin disruption may be able to alleviate these distortions.
evidence: This statement is a speculation about future improvements.

claim: Epitope-preserving ExCel has a lower expansion isotropy compared to standard ExCel because its epitope-friendly treatment is not as effective in mechanically homogenizing the cuticle and/or the internal worm tissue.
source: Epitope-preserving ExCel has a lower expansion isotropy compared to standard ExCel, because its epitope-friendly treatment, which combines collagenase and a heat-mediated denaturation, is not as effective in mechanically homogenizing the cuticle and/or the internal worm tissue, as the standard, epitope-disruptive, Proteinase K treatment.
evidence: This statement explains the reason for lower isotropy in epitope-preserving ExCel.

claim: Iterative ExCel has a high isotropy that is on par with standard ExCel because it inherits the Proteinase K treatment from standard ExCel.
source: On the other hand, iterative ExCel has a high isotropy that is on par with standard ExCel, because it inherits the Proteinase K treatment from standard ExCel
evidence: This statement explains the reason for high isotropy in iterative ExCel.

claim: It would be feasible to perform three or more rounds of expansion using additional hydrogel crosslinkers compatible with DATD and bis.
source: Using additional hydrogel crosslinkers that are compatible with DATD and bis, it would be feasible to perform three or more rounds of expansion, as previously demonstrated in iExM (Chang et al., 2017), which could further improve theoretical limits of resolution.
evidence: This statement is a speculation about future improvements with a citation.

claim: Expansion microscopy protocols are continuously being extended to include greater multiplexing capability for both RNA imaging and protein imaging.
source: Expansion microscopy protocols are continuously being extended, to include greater multiplexing capability for both RNA imaging (Chen et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2018) and protein imaging (Ku et al., 2016)
evidence: This statement describes ongoing developments with citations.

claim: These augmentations could in principle be applied to ExCel as well.
source: These augmentations could in principle be applied to ExCel as well.
evidence: This statement is a speculation about future applications.

claim: ExCel and its variant protocols might facilitate the reconstruction of a molecularly annotated connectome of a single entire animal.
source: For example, if combined with a high-density membrane stain and antibodies against synaptic proteins, ExCel and its variant protocols, such as iterative ExCel with three or more rounds of hydrogel expansion, might facilitate the reconstruction of a molecularly annotated connectome (i.e. with molecular information at each synapse) of a single entire animal
evidence: This statement is a speculation about future applications.
